in_english.long_meaning: Hawis is a term used in Islamic scholarship to describe an expert who interprets and comments on the Quran and Hadith. The name is derived from the Arabic root ه-ا-و-س meaning 'one who knows' or 'one who understands'. In Islamic tradition, Hawis refers to a scholar who possesses deep knowledge and understanding of the Quran and Hadith, enabling them to provide insightful commentary and interpretation. The term is often associated with the Sahabah, the companions of the Prophet Muhammad, who were renowned for their expertise in Islamic scholarship. In modern times, the name Hawis is given to children born into Muslim families, symbolizing the parents' desire for their child to grow up as a learned and knowledgeable individual who can contribute to the Islamic community through their scholarship and interpretation.
